paper.central_claim: Closing the loop at the level of the control code within an episode (a frozen VLM re-observes multi-view RGB, proprioception and state delta every K steps and rewrites the Python control function) lifts a training-free, zero-demonstration policy from 3.5% to 35.1% pooled success on a 57-task MuJoCo/RoboVerse sweep, the gain traced to 27.3% within-episode recovery of failed grasps, at about 10 cache-warm VLM calls per episode.
paper.title: VLCP: Vision Language Control Policy Closed-Loop Code Replanning for Robot Manipulation

signatures.object: Control function (Python control(obs,J)->joint targets) written by a frozen frontier VLM (GPT-5.5); baseline is the same system queried once per episode (K=T).
signatures.information: Multi-view RGB (two fixed cameras) at the live turn only, proprioception, a numeric state delta, previous block's code and action dicts; privileged object poses from the simulator; analytic Jacobian handed to code as an IK primitive. Not available: learned detector output, real sensing.
signatures.operation: Every K=50 steps the VLM is re-queried and emits a new control function (and optional skill modules) for the next block; the compiled function runs closed-loop on obs/J within the block.
signatures.output: Next-block control code plus helper skill modules; actions are per-joint position targets for a PD controller.
signatures.conditions: Simulation only; strong frozen VLM required (Qwen3-4B failed); 500-step horizon (about 10 replans); binary terminal predicate from LIBERO tasks.
signatures.feedback: Observation is the VLM's own reading of images, a numeric summary and the previous code/trace; there is no external verifier of intermediate code beyond compile/import and runtime exceptions.
signatures.selection_rule: None: each new block replaces the old function; there is no candidate comparison, acceptance gate or rollback of the control function.
signatures.persistence: Within the episode: history of up to 20 replan pairs with images dropped from history. Across episodes: skill modules saved to control_policies/skills/, up to 12 most recent injected verbatim into later prompts; the library is reset per task in the sweep.
signatures.later_use: Skills are imported by later control functions; not exercised across tasks in the reported sweep.
signatures.claimed_effect: 3.5% -> 35.1% pooled success versus K=T; 27.3% (15/55) of failed grasps recovered by a later replan.
signatures.failure_boundary: 40/55 failed-grasp episodes never recover; long-horizon tasks fall to 23.5%; replan latency 18.8 s median; no real robot; perception noise untested.

signatures.object: Cross-episode skill library of VLM-written helper modules (secondary claim).
signatures.information: Source text of previously written modules; only import success is checked (failed import reverts the file and surfaces the error).
signatures.operation: Extract labelled helper blocks written during any replan, write atomically to disk, re-inject up to 12 by recency into Block B of later system prompts.
signatures.output: Importable skill functions available to later control functions.
signatures.conditions: Shared directory with process lock; no curation, promotion criteria or curriculum.
signatures.selection_rule: Recency cap of 12; no quality or success filter.
signatures.claimed_effect: Described as an outlook for continual learning; no measurement of reuse or gains is reported.
signatures.failure_boundary: Not evaluated: the main sweep resets the library per task, so there is no retained-improvement evidence.

gap.author_gap: Code-generation methods write the program once and cannot recover from runtime failures; monitoring/replanning methods retry a fixed policy or reselect a subtask but never rewrite the failing code; VLAs expose no point for mid-execution reasoning.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and specific: a failed grasp rides to the end of an open-loop code policy (open-loop success 3.5%). The distinction between rewriting code and retrying/subtask-replanning is asserted through a feature table (Table 1) but is not tested against any such alternative.
lineage: Code as Policies / ProgPrompt / ELLMER (single query before execution)
Code-as-Monitor / DoReMi / Inner Monologue (monitor then retry or escalate)
Act-Observe-Rewrite 2603.04466 (rewrites controller between trials; closest ancestor per authors)
gap.closest_adjacent: Act-Observe-Rewrite rewrites between trials; CaP-Agent0 already rewrites within an episode on a different benchmark (LIBERO-PRO). Neither is run on the authors' sweep; the 18-22% CaP-Agent0 figure is quoted across benchmarks.
gap.residue: Within-episode recovery of manipulation failures by editing code; granularity of recovery on tasks with no plan-level correlate.
gap.stakes: Failed grasps are terminal for single-shot code policies; success collapses to near zero in every scene family.
gap.method_response: Re-query a frozen VLM every K steps with live images and a state delta, rewriting the control function; add a persistent skill library.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether code-level rewriting matters versus any VLM replanning with re-observation; real-world perception; K sensitivity; the skill library's effect; multi-seed variance.
unresolved: Gap is substantiated mainly against the method's own degenerate case; difference from the concurrent CaP-Agent0 is unmeasured.

tactic_steps_checked: 1 boundary: VLM writes policy code, executor/IK primitive and PD controller run it (seam named: reasoning vs motion)
2 artifact: executable Python control function (machine-checkable by compile/run)
3 loop closure: execution trace and re-observation feed the next rewrite, mid-episode
4 ablation: K=T collapses to the open-loop baseline (executed, but isolates frequency, not code-vs-other-artifact)
5 cost: calls, tokens, latency, cache reported; privileged poses disclosed

matches.reason: The learned model emits an executable control program that is run and re-generated from the execution result every K steps; this is the C25 operation 'structured artifact routed to a checker, loop closed during construction'. rs_pattern.reason: Primary decompose_and_delegate with C25 chosen over adapt_via_conditioning (C03 requires an upstream tuning phase teaching a model to parse a schema; VLCP only prompts a frozen model) and over reframe_as_solvable_object (no recast into a mature solver class).

executes_pattern.reason: Executable artifact and in-episode loop closure are executed; the checker is the same VLM, not a sound solver.

resolves_problem.reason: Open-loop failure is mitigated (3.5% -> 35.1% in sim with privileged poses) but 40 of 55 failed-grasp episodes never recover and no real-robot or alternative-loop evidence closes the problem.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: C25 'learned model emits executable program, solver/interpreter returns execution result' maps to a frozen VLM writing control code that the simulator runs; the K105 coding-runtime planner is replaced by a block-wise regeneration of one function.

claims.text: Within-episode code replanning (K=50) gives 35.1% pooled success versus 3.5% for the same system at K=T.
claims.setting: 57 LIBERO-derived tasks (10 Object Picks, 30 Kitchen, 17 Living-Room), MuJoCo/RoboVerse Franka, GPT-5.5, privileged poses, 500-step horizon, one episode per task.
claims.baseline: Same system with K=T (single query), model/API/poses/budget fixed.
claims.selection_vs_test: No separate selection set; development use of these tasks is not reported.
counterevidence: Open-loop comparator also receives only one VLM call; more compute/tokens in the closed-loop arm are not controlled.
claims.allowed_conclusion: In this simulator with privileged poses, giving the same frozen model repeated re-observation and rewrite opportunities greatly improves over single-shot code; it does not establish that the code-level locus is the key factor.

claims.text: The gain is explained by within-episode recovery: 27.3% of failed grasps are re-approached and lifted by a later replan.
claims.setting: 75 closed-loop pick-and-place episodes (a superset including reframing-study episodes), logged traces.
claims.baseline: K=T recovery set to 0 by construction.
claims.result: 55/75 episodes with a failed grasp; 15 recover; median 3 replans after the miss.
counterevidence: Detector thresholds are heuristic and unvalidated; baseline recovery is not measured; denominator differs from the sweep.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Recovery transitions occur in a minority of failed episodes and are consistent with the claimed mechanism; the contribution to the 3.5% -> 35.1% gap is not quantified.

claims.text: The loop is affordable: about 10 compact VLM calls per episode with 84% cache hits.
claims.result: median 10 replans, 43k input tokens, 349 output tokens, 18.8 s latency per replan.
counterevidence: 18.8 s per replan limits reactive control; no USD cost; K not swept.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Token cost is measured and moderate; practical suitability is limited to slow manipulation.

claims.text: VLCP is robust to instruction reframing whereas VLA-0 is not (pooled 40.0% unchanged vs 97.3% -> 75.0%).
claims.setting: 6 LIBERO-Object tasks, N=10 per VLCP cell, 10 per modified VLA-0 task.
claims.baseline: VLA-0 fine-tuned on LIBERO (an upper reference, not matched).
claims.result: VLCP 40.0% both conditions; VLA-0 collapses on butter (96%->0%).
counterevidence: VLA-0 stays far above VLCP in-distribution; N=10; authors call it indicative.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Closed-loop success judged by the benchmark predicate in simulation; no real robot; dev/test separation not reported so no transfer is granted.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In MuJoCo/RoboVerse with privileged object poses, repeated VLM re-observation and rewrite of the control function (K=50) raises single-episode success per task from 2/57 to 20/57 relative to a single-query version of the same system, with a logged failed-grasp recovery rate of 15/55; token cost is moderate.
unresolved: Whether editing code is better than retrying a fixed policy or reselecting a subtask.
Contribution of images versus privileged poses.

status_reason: Full text including appendices read; all eight items judged from the pinned material.

evidence.quote: VLCP’s central claim is that recovering from an execution failure means closing the loop at the level of the control code , within the episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Author central claim: the closed loop must act on the control code itself inside one episode.

evidence.quote: At the start of each block the VLM is queried once to generate a new control function, which then runs for every remaining step in the block with no further VLM queries.
evidence.support_explanation: Operation: frozen VLM rewrites the control function every K steps; between replans the compiled function runs unchanged.

evidence.quote: Since VLCP is handed privileged object poses, it is fair to ask what the RGB observations are for.
evidence.support_explanation: Information: object poses are privileged simulator state; RGB is claimed to drive failure diagnosis, but no no-image ablation exists.

evidence.quote: Each task runs for a single episode, with the skill library reset beforehand to keep trials independent
evidence.support_explanation: Denominator: one episode per task; the skill library is reset, so cross-episode reuse is not exercised in the main sweep.

evidence.quote: closed-loop VLCP reaches 60.0\% on Object Picks, 33.3\% on Kitchen Scenes, and 23.5\% on Living-Room Scenes, pooling to 35.1\% [ 24.0 , 48.1 ] overall.
evidence.support_explanation: Main closed-loop result over the 57-task sweep with Wilson CI.

evidence.quote: Set to K{=}T , the same system collapses to 10.0\% , 3.3\% , and 0.0\% , or 3.5\% [ 1.0 , 11.9 ] pooled.
evidence.support_explanation: Matched open-loop (K=T) comparator result.

evidence.quote: The ablation shares VLCP’s simulator, control API, privileged object poses, task set, model, and episode budget, so any difference traces to the replanning loop alone
evidence.support_explanation: Control: matched K=T ablation; it varies re-querying frequency, not code-level rewriting versus other replan granularities.

evidence.quote: Of the 75 episodes, 55 contain at least one failed grasp.
evidence.support_explanation: Recovery denominator: 55 episodes with a failed grasp; 15 recover (27.3%).

evidence.quote: we label a block a failed grasp when the hand is at the object (end-effector–object distance below 0.13 m) with the gripper closed but the object still on the surface
evidence.support_explanation: The recovery detector is a hand-set threshold heuristic on logged state, not validated against labels.

evidence.quote: Open-loop ( K{=}T ) recovery is 0 by construction, since it never re-observes.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline recovery is assumed zero rather than measured.

evidence.quote: End-to-end latency for a single replan is a median of 18.8 s (mean 25.9 s)
evidence.support_explanation: Measured cost: median ~10 calls/episode, 84% cache hit, 18.8 s per replan.

evidence.quote: we read the modified-task comparison as indicative rather than statistically conclusive at this sample size
evidence.support_explanation: Instruction-reframing study uses N=10 per cell and a VLA-0 reference that is not matched.

evidence.quote: VLCP relies on simulator-provided object poses and has only been run in simulation
evidence.support_explanation: Scope limit: simulation only, privileged poses.

evidence.quote: the main sweep runs a single episode per task (Section 4.1 ), and we lean on per-family pooling and Wilson confidence intervals rather than multi-seed repetition.
evidence.support_explanation: Statistics limit acknowledged by the authors.

evidence.quote: We did not sweep K ; a systematic study of the cadence–cost trade-off
evidence.support_explanation: Replan cadence K=50 is a single untested setting.

evidence.quote: The closest work, Act-Observe-Rewrite [ 7 ] , does rewrite the full controller, but between trials
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest neighbour for gap: rewrites controller between trials, not within episode.

evidence.quote: Concurrent work, CaP-Agent0 [ 2 ] , reaches the same design point from the benchmarking side
evidence.support_explanation: A concurrent method occupies the same design cell; no empirical comparison on the same benchmark.

evidence.quote: Skill files persist across episodes and are shared across concurrent LLMPolicy instances, coordinated with a process-level lock.
evidence.support_explanation: Persistence of the skill library; later prompts import saved skills.

evidence.quote: The smaller open models we tried (Qwen3-4B) failed to produce reliable control code or effective replanning
evidence.support_explanation: The method depends on a strong frozen VLM (GPT-5.5).

evidence.quote: VLA-0 is evaluated over 50 episodes per original task and 10 per modified task, VLCP over 10 episodes per task variant in both conditions.
evidence.support_explanation: Unequal episode counts across arms in the reframing study.

evidence.quote: All 778 generated control blocks across every episode parsed and compiled successfully
evidence.support_explanation: Code validity is not the bottleneck.

evidence.quote: VLCP uses GPT-5.5 as the replanning model, queried every K{=}50 steps as described in Section 3 .
evidence.support_explanation: Base model GPT-5.5 is fixed across arms.

G.reason: Specific bottleneck (silent failures in single-shot code) with named nearest neighbours and a clearly drawn residual; the claimed novelty over the concurrent CaP-Agent0 and over retry/subtask replanning is not tested.

M.reason: Operation, information and the reason the failure lives in code are reconstructable and the K=T degenerate case gives a distinguishing prediction (zero recovery); the claim that images drive diagnosis is untested and K is not swept.

X.reason: Prompt layout, block cadence, history cap, import/revert rule, skill injection and format contract are specified with appendix assets; the skill library is not exercised (reset per task) and there is no acceptance/rollback of rewrites.

E.measurement.reason: Success is the benchmark's binary terminal predicate; recovery is derived from logged state but with an unvalidated 0.13 m threshold, and the baseline recovery is zero by construction. Denominators (57, 75, 81) are stated.

E.causality.reason: The matched K=T ablation isolates re-querying frequency but not code-level rewriting, image use, retry/subtask alternatives or compute (about 10 vs 1 call); no skill-library or image ablation.

E.holdout.reason: No development/test separation, contamination or task-overlap statement for the 57 LIBERO tasks and prompt examples; one simulator/embodiment, privileged poses; the reframing study varies wording only on six tasks.

E.statistics.reason: Wilson CIs with non-overlapping per-family intervals, failure denominators for recovery (55, 40 non-recovering); but one episode per task, no repeats or paired tests, N=10 cells in the reframing study.

E.cost.reason: Calls, tokens, cache fraction and latency measured from logs; the cost of the comparator (one call) is lower, so budgets are not matched, and no USD or K trade-off is reported.
